ko.title: 48.1의 심리 지표: 미국인들이 데이터가 시사하는 것보다 더 우울함을 느끼는 이유

segments.src: When the University of Michigan released its final consumer sentiment reading for September, the headline number landed near 48.
segments.tr: 미시간대학교가 9월 최종 소비자 심리 지수를 발표했을 때, 헤드라인 수치는 48 부근을 기록했습니다.

segments.src: By historical standards, that is a very low reading, the kind of level more often associated with deep recessions or acute inflation shocks than with an economy that is still adding jobs and growing.
segments.tr: 역사적 기준으로 볼 때 이는 매우 낮은 수치이며, 여전히 일자리가 늘어나고 성장하는 경제보다는 심각한 경기 침체나 극심한 인플레이션 충격과 더 자주 연관되는 수준입니다.

segments.src: The survey also showed year-ahead inflation expectations climbing toward 4.6%.
segments.tr: 또한 이번 조사에서는 향후 1년 기대 인플레이션이 4.6%를 향해 상승하는 것으로 나타났습니다.

segments.src: For many observers, the pairing raises an old question: why does the mood of American households so often diverge from the hard economic data?
segments.tr: 많은 관측통들에게 이러한 조합은 오래된 의문을 제기합니다. 왜 미국 가계의 분위기는 객관적인 경제 데이터와 이처럼 자주 엇갈릴까요?

segments.src: And, just as importantly, why do central bankers pay such close attention to it?
segments.tr: 그리고 그만큼 중요한 점은, 왜 중앙은행들이 이 지표에 그토록 주의를 기울이는가 하는 점입니다.

segments.src: ## What the Index Actually Measures
segments.tr: ## 지수가 실제로 측정하는 것

segments.src: The University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers asks a representative sample of households about their personal finances, their view of business conditions, and their buying plans.
segments.tr: 미시간대학교 소비자 조사(University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers)는 대표적인 가계 표본을 대상으로 개인 재정 상황, 경기 여건에 대한 전망, 그리고 구매 계획을 묻습니다.

segments.src: Respondents are also asked what they expect to happen to prices over the next year and over the next five to ten years.
segments.tr: 또한 응답자들에게 향후 1년 동안 그리고 향후 5~10년 동안 물가가 어떻게 변동할 것으로 예상하는지도 질문합니다.

segments.src: Two points are worth keeping in mind:
segments.tr: 기억해 둘 만한 두 가지 포인트가 있습니다:

segments.src: - **It measures perception, not activity.** The index captures how people feel, not how much they are spending or earning.
segments.tr: - **이것은 활동이 아니라 인식을 측정합니다.** 이 지수는 사람들이 얼마나 지출하거나 벌고 있는지가 아니라 어떻게 느끼는지를 포착합니다.

segments.src: - **It is a diffusion-style index.** A reading near 48 does not mean "48% of people are unhappy." It reflects the balance of favorable and unfavorable answers, scaled against a baseline year.
segments.tr: - **확산형(diffusion-style) 지수입니다.** 48 부근의 수치는 "사람들의 48%가 불행하다"는 뜻이 아닙니다. 기준 연도와 비교하여 우호적 답변과 비우호적 답변의 균형을 반영합니다.

segments.src: ## Why Mood and Data Keep Pulling Apart
segments.tr: ## 심리와 데이터가 계속 벌어지는 이유

segments.src: Economists have offered several explanations for the gap between sentiment and statistics.
segments.tr: 경제학자들은 심리와 통계 사이의 격차에 대해 여러 가지 설명을 제시해 왔습니다.

segments.src: None of them is complete on its own, but together they paint a useful picture.
segments.tr: 그 어떤 설명도 그 자체만으로는 완벽하지 않지만, 종합하면 유용한 그림을 그려줍니다.

segments.src: ### 1. Price levels matter more than inflation rates
segments.tr: ### 1. 인플레이션율보다 물가 수준이 더 중요합니다

segments.src: Official statistics usually report the *rate* of inflation.
segments.tr: 공식 통계는 대개 인플레이션의 *증가율*을 보고합니다.

segments.src: Households, however, experience the *level* of prices.
segments.tr: 그러나 가계는 물가의 *절대적인 수준*을 체감합니다.

segments.src: Even if inflation cools, groceries, rent, insurance, and utilities may still cost far more than they did a few years ago.
segments.tr: 비록 인플레이션이 진정되더라도 식료품, 월세, 보험료, 공과금은 몇 년 전보다 여전히 훨씬 더 비쌀 수 있습니다.

segments.src: People tend to judge their well-being against what they remember paying, not against a rate of change.
segments.tr: 사람들은 변화율이 아니라 자신이 기억하는 지불 금액을 기준으로 자신의 안녕을 판단하는 경향이 있습니다.

segments.src: ### 2. Frequent purchases shape perception
segments.tr: ### 2. 빈번한 구매가 인식을 형성합니다

segments.src: Gasoline, food, and other everyday items are bought often and are highly visible.
segments.tr: 휘발유, 식료품 및 기타 일상용품은 자주 구매되며 가시성이 높습니다.

segments.src: Big-ticket price moves in these categories can color a household's overall view of the economy more than a broad price index does.
segments.tr: 이러한 범주의 가격 변동은 광범위한 물가 지수보다 가계의 전반적인 경제관에 더 큰 영향을 미칠 수 있습니다.

segments.src: ### 3. Borrowing costs bite
segments.tr: ### 3. 차입 비용의 압박

segments.src: Higher interest rates affect mortgages, auto loans, and credit cards.
segments.tr: 더 높은 금리는 모기지, 자동차 대출, 신용카드에 영향을 미칩니다.

segments.src: Someone who wants to buy a home or finance a car may feel squeezed even while the broader economy looks resilient.
segments.tr: 주택을 구매하거나 자동차 할부를 받으려는 사람은 광범위한 경제가 회복력 있어 보이는 동안에도 압박을 느낄 수 있습니다.

segments.src: That experience can weigh heavily on answers about "good times to buy."
segments.tr: 그러한 경험은 "구매하기 좋은 시기"에 대한 답변에 큰 무게를 싣게 됩니다.

segments.src: ### 4. Uneven experiences hide behind averages
segments.tr: ### 4. 평균 뒤에 숨겨진 불균일한 경험

segments.src: Aggregate data can look healthy while particular groups, such as renters, younger workers, or lower-income households, face a different reality.
segments.tr: 종합 데이터는 건강해 보일 수 있지만, 세입자, 젊은 노동자, 저소득층 가구와 같은 특정 그룹은 전혀 다른 현실에 직면해 있습니다.

segments.src: Sentiment surveys can pick up that unevenness in a way that headline employment or output figures do not.
segments.tr: 심리 조사는 헤드라인 고용이나 생산 수치가 포착하지 못하는 방식으로 이러한 불균일성을 포착할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: ### 5. Information and political filters
segments.tr: ### 5. 정보와 정치적 필터

segments.src: Research has consistently shown that views about the economy can vary with political affiliation, media consumption, and recent news.
segments.tr: 연구에 따르면 경제에 대한 견해는 정치적 성향, 미디어 소비, 최근 뉴스의 영향을 받아 다양하게 나타날 수 있습니다.

segments.src: The same data can be read very differently depending on the lens.
segments.tr: 어떤 렌즈를 통해 보느냐에 따라 동일한 데이터도 완전히 다르게 해석될 수 있습니다.

segments.src: ## Why Expectations Matter for the Fed
segments.tr: ## 연준에게 기대치가 중요한 이유

segments.src: The most closely watched part of the report for policymakers may not be the headline index at all.
segments.tr: 정책 입안자들이 보고서에서 가장 주시하는 부분은 헤드라인 지수가 아닐 수도 있습니다.

segments.src: It is the inflation expectations component.
segments.tr: 바로 인플레이션 기대치 구성 요소입니다.

segments.src: Central banks generally believe that what people *expect* inflation to be can influence what inflation actually becomes.
segments.tr: 중앙은행들은 대개 사람들이 인플레이션이 어떻게 될 것이라고 *예상*하는지가 실제 인플레이션이 되는 데 영향을 미칠 수 있다고 믿습니다.

segments.src: If households expect prices to rise faster, they may push for higher wages, accept price increases more readily, or move purchases forward.
segments.tr: 가계가 물가가 더 빨리 오를 것으로 예상하면 더 높은 임금을 요구하거나, 가격 인상을 더 쉽게 수용하거나, 구매를 앞당길 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Businesses that expect rising costs may raise prices sooner.
segments.tr: 상승하는 비용을 예상하는 기업은 가격을 더 빨리 인상할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: Over time, these behaviors can make elevated inflation more persistent.
segments.tr: 시간이 지남에 따라 이러한 행동은 높은 인플레이션을 더욱 고착화할 수 있습니다.

segments.src: That is why a move in year-ahead expectations toward 4.6% draws attention.
segments.tr: 그렇기 때문에 향후 1년 기대치가 4.6%를 향해 움직이는 것에 주의를 기울이는 것입니다.

segments.src: Several caveats apply:
segments.tr: 몇 가지 유의 사항이 적용됩니다:

segments.src: - **Short-term expectations are noisy.** Year-ahead figures can swing with gasoline prices and news headlines, and they often overstate where inflation eventually settles.
segments.tr: - **단기 기대치는 노이즈가 많습니다.** 향후 1년 수치는 휘발유 가격과 뉴스 헤드라인에 따라 흔들릴 수 있으며, 인플레이션이 결국 안착하는 지점을 과장하는 경우가 많습니다.

segments.src: - **Longer-term expectations matter more.** The Federal Reserve typically watches whether expectations five to ten years out remain "anchored" near its stated 2% goal. A rise there would be considered more concerning than a short-run jump.
segments.tr: - **장기 기대치가 더 중요합니다.** 연방준비제도는 주로 5년에서 10년 후의 기대치가 명시된 2% 목표치 부근에 "고정(anchored)"되어 유지되는지 관찰합니다. 그곳의 상승은 단기적인 급등보다 더 우려스러운 것으로 간주됩니다.

segments.src: - **Survey and market measures can disagree.** Policymakers compare household surveys with market-based indicators and other surveys of professional forecasters before drawing conclusions.
segments.tr: - **조사 지표와 시장 지표가 엇갈릴 수 있습니다.** 정책 입안자들은 결론을 내리기 전에 가계 설문조사를 시장 기반 지표 및 전문 전망가들의 다른 설문조사와 비교합니다.

segments.src: ## What to Watch Next
segments.tr: ## 다음으로 주시해야 할 것

segments.src: A single monthly reading does not define a trend.
segments.tr: 단 한 달의 수치가 추세를 정의하지는 않습니다.

segments.src: Readers who want to understand where sentiment may go from here could keep an eye on:
segments.tr: 심리가 앞으로 어디로 향할지 이해하고자 하는 독자들은 다음 사항을 주시할 수 있습니다:

segments.src: 1. **Gasoline and grocery prices**, which tend to feed quickly into household expectations.
segments.tr: 1. **휘발유 및 식료품 가격**, 이는 가계의 기대치에 빠르게 반영되는 경향이 있습니다.

segments.src: 2. **Labor market conditions**, since job security is a major driver of confidence.
segments.tr: 2. **노동 시장 여건**, 고용 안정성은 신뢰의 주요 동인(driver)이기 때문입니다.

segments.src: 3. **Longer-run inflation expectations**, which are more important to monetary policy than the one-year figure.
segments.tr: 3. **장기 인플레이션 기대치**, 이는 통화 정책에 있어서 1년짜리 수치보다 더 중요합니다.

segments.src: 4. **Other confidence gauges**, such as the Conference Board's index, which uses a different methodology and sometimes tells a different story.
segments.tr: 4. **기타 신뢰도 지표**, 서로 다른 방법론을 사용하여 때로는 다른 이야기를 전달하는 콘퍼런스보드(The Conference Board)의 지수 등.

segments.src: ## The Bottom Line
segments.tr: ## 핵심 요약

segments.src: A sentiment reading near 48 is a signal about how people feel, and feelings are part of the economy.
segments.tr: 48 부근의 심리 지표는 사람들이 어떻게 느끼는지에 대한 신호이며, 감정은 경제의 일부입니다.

segments.src: Households that feel pessimistic may spend more cautiously, and expectations that drift higher can complicate the job of those responsible for price stability.
segments.tr: 비관적으로 느끼는 가계는 더 신중하게 지출할 수 있으며, 더 높아진 기대치는 물가 안정을 책임지는 사람들의 일을 복잡하게 만들 수 있습니다.

segments.src: At the same time, sentiment is not a forecast, and it has often been a poor predictor of near-term spending.
segments.tr: 동시에 심리는 예측이 아니며, 단기 지출의 형편없는 예측 지표인 경우가 많았습니다.

segments.src: The gap between the mood and the data is not necessarily a contradiction.
segments.tr: 분위기와 데이터 사이의 격차가 반드시 모순인 것은 아닙니다.

segments.src: It is a reminder that an economy is both a set of statistics and a set of lived experiences, and that policymakers have to take both seriously.
segments.tr: 이는 경제가 일련의 통계이자 일련의 삶의 경험이기도 하며, 정책 입안자들은 둘 다 심각하게 받아들여야 한다는 점을 상기시켜 줍니다.

hi.title: 48.1 की उपभोक्ता भावना रीडिंग: अमेरिकी लोग डेटा की तुलना में अधिक निराश क्यों महसूस कर रहे हैं

segments.src: When the University of Michigan released its final consumer sentiment reading for September, the headline number landed near 48.
segments.tr: जब मिशिगन विश्वविद्यालय ने सितंबर के लिए अपनी अंतिम उपभोक्ता भावना (कंज्यूमर सेंटीमेंट) रीडिंग जारी की, तो मुख्य आंकड़ा 48 के करीब रहा।

segments.src: By historical standards, that is a very low reading, the kind of level more often associated with deep recessions or acute inflation shocks than with an economy that is still adding jobs and growing.
segments.tr: ऐतिहासिक मानकों के अनुसार, यह एक बहुत ही कम रीडिंग है, इस तरह का स्तर आमतौर पर नौकरियों के बढ़ने और विकास कर रही अर्थव्यवस्था के बजाय गहरी मंदी या तीव्र मुद्रास्फीति के झटकों से जुड़ा होता है।

segments.src: The survey also showed year-ahead inflation expectations climbing toward 4.6%.
segments.tr: सर्वेक्षण ने अगले एक साल की मुद्रास्फीति की उम्मीदों को भी 4.6% की ओर बढ़ते हुए दिखाया।

segments.src: For many observers, the pairing raises an old question: why does the mood of American households so often diverge from the hard economic data?
segments.tr: कई विश्लेषकों के लिए, यह संयोजन एक पुराना सवाल खड़ा करता है: अमेरिकी परिवारों का मूड अक्सर वास्तविक आर्थिक आंकड़ों से अलग क्यों हो जाता है?

segments.src: And, just as importantly, why do central bankers pay such close attention to it?
segments.tr: और, उतना ही महत्वपूर्ण यह भी है कि केंद्रीय बैंक इस पर इतना ध्यान क्यों देते हैं?

segments.src: ## What the Index Actually Measures
segments.tr: ## सूचकांक वास्तव में क्या मापता है

segments.src: The University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers asks a representative sample of households about their personal finances, their view of business conditions, and their buying plans.
segments.tr: मिशिगन विश्वविद्यालय का उपभोक्ता सर्वेक्षण परिवारों के एक प्रतिनिधि नमूने से उनके व्यक्तिगत वित्त, व्यावसायिक स्थितियों पर उनके दृष्टिकोण और उनकी खरीदारी योजनाओं के बारे में पूछता है।

segments.src: Respondents are also asked what they expect to happen to prices over the next year and over the next five to ten years.
segments.tr: उत्तरदाताओं से यह भी पूछा जाता है कि वे अगले एक वर्ष और अगले पांच से दस वर्षों में कीमतों में क्या बदलाव की उम्मीद करते हैं।

segments.src: Two points are worth keeping in mind:
segments.tr: दो बिंदुओं को ध्यान में रखना महत्वपूर्ण है:

segments.src: - **It measures perception, not activity.** The index captures how people feel, not how much they are spending or earning.
segments.tr: - **यह धारणा को मापता है, गतिविधि को नहीं।** सूचकांक यह दर्शाता है कि लोग कैसा महसूस करते हैं, न कि वे कितना खर्च कर रहे हैं या कमा रहे हैं।

segments.src: - **It is a diffusion-style index.** A reading near 48 does not mean "48% of people are unhappy." It reflects the balance of favorable and unfavorable answers, scaled against a baseline year.
segments.tr: - **यह एक प्रसार-शैली (diffusion-style) का सूचकांक है।** 48 के करीब रीडिंग का मतलब यह नहीं है कि "48% लोग नाखुश हैं।" यह अनुकूल और प्रतिकूल उत्तरों के संतुलन को दर्शाता है, जिसे एक आधार वर्ष के मुकाबले मापा जाता है।

segments.src: ## Why Mood and Data Keep Pulling Apart
segments.tr: ## मूड और डेटा लगातार अलग क्यों हो रहे हैं

segments.src: Economists have offered several explanations for the gap between sentiment and statistics.
segments.tr: अर्थशास्त्रियों ने उपभोक्ता भावना और आंकड़ों के बीच के अंतर के लिए कई स्पष्टीकरण दिए हैं।

segments.src: None of them is complete on its own, but together they paint a useful picture.
segments.tr: उनमें से कोई भी अपने आप में पूर्ण नहीं है, लेकिन साथ मिलकर वे एक उपयोगी तस्वीर पेश करते हैं।

segments.src: ### 1. Price levels matter more than inflation rates
segments.tr: ### 1. मुद्रास्फीति की दरों से अधिक कीमतों का स्तर मायने रखता है

segments.src: Official statistics usually report the *rate* of inflation.
segments.tr: आधिकारिक आंकड़े आमतौर पर मुद्रास्फीति की *दर* की रिपोर्ट करते हैं।

segments.src: Households, however, experience the *level* of prices.
segments.tr: हालाँकि, परिवार कीमतों के *स्तर* का अनुभव करते हैं।

segments.src: Even if inflation cools, groceries, rent, insurance, and utilities may still cost far more than they did a few years ago.
segments.tr: भले ही मुद्रास्फीति ठंडी हो जाए, फिर भी किराने का सामान, किराया, बीमा और उपयोगिताओं (utilities) की कीमत कुछ साल पहले की तुलना में बहुत अधिक हो सकती है।

segments.src: People tend to judge their well-being against what they remember paying, not against a rate of change.
segments.tr: लोग अपने कल्याण का आकलन बदलाव की दर के बजाय उस कीमत के आधार पर करते हैं जो उन्हें याद है कि वे पहले चुकाते थे।

segments.src: ### 2. Frequent purchases shape perception
segments.tr: ### 2. बार-बार की जाने वाली खरीदारी धारणा को आकार देती है

segments.src: Gasoline, food, and other everyday items are bought often and are highly visible.
segments.tr: पेट्रोल, भोजन और अन्य दैनिक उपयोग की वस्तुएं अक्सर खरीदी जाती हैं और अत्यधिक दिखाई देती हैं।

segments.src: Big-ticket price moves in these categories can color a household's overall view of the economy more than a broad price index does.
segments.tr: इन श्रेणियों में बड़ी कीमतों का उतार-चढ़ाव एक व्यापक मूल्य सूचकांक की तुलना में अर्थव्यवस्था के बारे में परिवार के समग्र दृष्टिकोण को अधिक प्रभावित कर सकता है।

segments.src: ### 3. Borrowing costs bite
segments.tr: ### 3. कर्ज की लागत का असर

segments.src: Higher interest rates affect mortgages, auto loans, and credit cards.
segments.tr: उच्च ब्याज दरें बंधक (mortgages), ऑटो ऋण और क्रेडिट कार्ड को प्रभावित करती हैं।

segments.src: Someone who wants to buy a home or finance a car may feel squeezed even while the broader economy looks resilient.
segments.tr: जो व्यक्ति घर खरीदना चाहता है या कार के लिए ऋण लेना चाहता है, वह व्यापक अर्थव्यवस्था के मजबूत दिखने के बावजूद दबाव महसूस कर सकता है।

segments.src: That experience can weigh heavily on answers about "good times to buy."
segments.tr: वह अनुभव "खरीदारी के लिए अच्छे समय" के बारे में उत्तरों पर भारी पड़ सकता है।

segments.src: ### 4. Uneven experiences hide behind averages
segments.tr: ### 4. औसतों के पीछे असमान अनुभव छिपे होते हैं

segments.src: Aggregate data can look healthy while particular groups, such as renters, younger workers, or lower-income households, face a different reality.
segments.tr: समग्र आंकड़े स्वस्थ दिख सकते हैं जबकि विशेष समूह, जैसे कि किराएदार, युवा कर्मचारी, या कम आय वाले परिवार, एक अलग वास्तविकता का सामना करते हैं।

segments.src: Sentiment surveys can pick up that unevenness in a way that headline employment or output figures do not.
segments.tr: उपभोक्ता भावना सर्वेक्षण उस असमानता को इस तरह से पकड़ सकते हैं जो मुख्य रोजगार या उत्पादन के आंकड़े नहीं कर पाते।

segments.src: ### 5. Information and political filters
segments.tr: ### 5. सूचना और राजनीतिक फिल्टर

segments.src: Research has consistently shown that views about the economy can vary with political affiliation, media consumption, and recent news.
segments.tr: शोध ने लगातार दिखाया है कि अर्थव्यवस्था के बारे में विचार राजनीतिक संबद्धता, मीडिया के उपभोग और हालिया समाचारों के साथ भिन्न हो सकते हैं।

segments.src: The same data can be read very differently depending on the lens.
segments.tr: एक ही डेटा को देखने के नजरिए के आधार पर बहुत अलग तरीके से पढ़ा जा सकता है।

segments.src: ## Why Expectations Matter for the Fed
segments.tr: ## फेड के लिए उम्मीदें क्यों मायने रखती हैं

segments.src: The most closely watched part of the report for policymakers may not be the headline index at all.
segments.tr: नीति निर्माताओं के लिए रिपोर्ट का सबसे बारीकी से देखा जाने वाला हिस्सा मुख्य सूचकांक नहीं भी हो सकता है।

segments.src: It is the inflation expectations component.
segments.tr: यह मुद्रास्फीति की उम्मीदों का घटक है।

segments.src: Central banks generally believe that what people *expect* inflation to be can influence what inflation actually becomes.
segments.tr: केंद्रीय बैंक आम तौर पर मानते हैं कि लोग मुद्रास्फीति के बारे में जो *उम्मीद* करते हैं, वह इस बात को प्रभावित कर सकती है कि मुद्रास्फीति वास्तव में क्या होगी।

segments.src: If households expect prices to rise faster, they may push for higher wages, accept price increases more readily, or move purchases forward.
segments.tr: यदि परिवारों को उम्मीद है कि कीमतें तेजी से बढ़ेंगी, तो वे अधिक वेतन की मांग कर सकते हैं, मूल्य वृद्धि को अधिक आसानी से स्वीकार कर सकते हैं, या खरीदारी को पहले कर सकते हैं।

segments.src: Businesses that expect rising costs may raise prices sooner.
segments.tr: बढ़ती लागत की उम्मीद करने वाले व्यवसाय कीमतों को जल्द ही बढ़ा सकते हैं।

segments.src: Over time, these behaviors can make elevated inflation more persistent.
segments.tr: समय के साथ, ये व्यवहार बढ़ी हुई मुद्रास्फीति को अधिक स्थायी बना सकते हैं।

segments.src: That is why a move in year-ahead expectations toward 4.6% draws attention.
segments.tr: यही कारण है कि अगले एक साल की उम्मीदों का 4.6% की ओर बढ़ना ध्यान आकर्षित करता है।

segments.src: Several caveats apply:
segments.tr: कई चेतावनियां लागू होती हैं:

segments.src: - **Short-term expectations are noisy.** Year-ahead figures can swing with gasoline prices and news headlines, and they often overstate where inflation eventually settles.
segments.tr: - **अल्पकालिक उम्मीदें अस्थिर होती हैं।** अगले एक साल के आंकड़े पेट्रोल की कीमतों और समाचारों की सुर्खियों के साथ बदल सकते हैं, और वे अक्सर उस स्तर को बढ़ा-चढ़ाकर पेश करते हैं जहां मुद्रास्फीति अंततः स्थिर होती है।

segments.src: - **Longer-term expectations matter more.** The Federal Reserve typically watches whether expectations five to ten years out remain "anchored" near its stated 2% goal. A rise there would be considered more concerning than a short-run jump.
segments.tr: - **दीर्घकालिक उम्मीदें अधिक मायने रखती हैं।** फेडरल रिजर्व आमतौर पर यह देखता है कि क्या पांच से दस साल की उम्मीदें उसके घोषित 2% के लक्ष्य के पास "स्थिर" बनी हुई हैं। वहां वृद्धि को अल्पकालिक उछाल की तुलना में अधिक चिंताजनक माना जाएगा।

segments.src: - **Survey and market measures can disagree.** Policymakers compare household surveys with market-based indicators and other surveys of professional forecasters before drawing conclusions.
segments.tr: - **सर्वेक्षण और बाजार के उपायों में असहमति हो सकती है।** नीति निर्माता निष्कर्ष निकालने से पहले घरेलू सर्वेक्षणों की तुलना बाजार-आधारित संकेतकों और पेशेवर पूर्वानुमानकर्ताओं के अन्य सर्वेक्षणों से करते हैं।

segments.src: ## What to Watch Next
segments.tr: ## आगे क्या देखना है

segments.src: A single monthly reading does not define a trend.
segments.tr: एक महीने की रीडिंग किसी प्रवृत्ति (trend) को परिभाषित नहीं करती है।

segments.src: Readers who want to understand where sentiment may go from here could keep an eye on:
segments.tr: जो पाठक यह समझना चाहते हैं कि यहाँ से भावना कहाँ जा सकती है, वे इन पर नज़र रख सकते हैं:

segments.src: 1. **Gasoline and grocery prices**, which tend to feed quickly into household expectations.
segments.tr: 1. **पेट्रोल और किराने की कीमतें**, जो घरेलू उम्मीदों को जल्दी प्रभावित करती हैं।

segments.src: 2. **Labor market conditions**, since job security is a major driver of confidence.
segments.tr: 2. **श्रम बाजार की स्थितियां**, क्योंकि नौकरी की सुरक्षा आत्मविश्वास का एक प्रमुख चालक है।

segments.src: 3. **Longer-run inflation expectations**, which are more important to monetary policy than the one-year figure.
segments.tr: 3. **दीर्घकालिक मुद्रास्फीति की उम्मीदें**, जो एक साल के आंकड़े की तुलना में मौद्रिक नीति के लिए अधिक महत्वपूर्ण हैं।

segments.src: 4. **Other confidence gauges**, such as the Conference Board's index, which uses a different methodology and sometimes tells a different story.
segments.tr: 4. **अन्य आत्मविश्वास के पैमाने**, जैसे कि कॉन्फ्रेंस बोर्ड का सूचकांक, जो एक अलग कार्यप्रणाली का उपयोग करता है और कभी-कभी एक अलग कहानी बयां करता है।

segments.src: ## The Bottom Line

es.title: Una lectura del sentimiento de 48.1: Por qué los estadounidenses se sienten más pesimistas de lo que sugieren los datos

segments.src: When the University of Michigan released its final consumer sentiment reading for September, the headline number landed near 48.
segments.tr: Cuando la Universidad de Michigan publicó su lectura final del sentimiento del consumidor para septiembre, la cifra principal se situó cerca de 48.

segments.src: By historical standards, that is a very low reading, the kind of level more often associated with deep recessions or acute inflation shocks than with an economy that is still adding jobs and growing.
segments.tr: Según los estándares históricos, se trata de una lectura muy baja, el tipo de nivel que se asocia más a menudo con recesiones profundas o shocks inflacionarios agudos que con una economía que sigue creando empleo y creciendo.

segments.src: The survey also showed year-ahead inflation expectations climbing toward 4.6%.
segments.tr: La encuesta también mostró que las expectativas de inflación para el próximo año suben hacia el 4.6%.

segments.src: For many observers, the pairing raises an old question: why does the mood of American households so often diverge from the hard economic data?
segments.tr: Para muchos observadores, esta combinación plantea una vieja pregunta: ¿por qué el estado de ánimo de los hogares estadounidenses diverge tan a menudo de los datos económicos duros?

segments.src: And, just as importantly, why do central bankers pay such close attention to it?
segments.tr: Y, lo que es igual de importante, ¿por qué los banqueros centrales le prestan tanta atención?

segments.src: ## What the Index Actually Measures
segments.tr: ## What the Index Actually Measures

segments.src: The University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers asks a representative sample of households about their personal finances, their view of business conditions, and their buying plans.
segments.tr: Las Encuestas de Consumidores de la Universidad de Michigan preguntan a una muestra representativa de hogares sobre sus finanzas personales, su opinión sobre las condiciones comerciales y sus planes de compra.

segments.src: Respondents are also asked what they expect to happen to prices over the next year and over the next five to ten years.
segments.tr: También se pregunta a los encuestados qué esperan que ocurra con los precios durante el próximo año y en los próximos cinco a diez años.

segments.src: Two points are worth keeping in mind:
segments.tr: Vale la pena tener en cuenta dos puntos:

segments.src: - **It measures perception, not activity.** The index captures how people feel, not how much they are spending or earning.
segments.tr: - **Mide la percepción, no la actividad.** El índice capta cómo se siente la gente, no cuánto está gastando o ganando.

segments.src: - **It is a diffusion-style index.** A reading near 48 does not mean "48% of people are unhappy." It reflects the balance of favorable and unfavorable answers, scaled against a baseline year.
segments.tr: - **Es un índice de tipo de difusión.** Una lectura cercana a 48 no significa que "el 48% de la gente esté infeliz". Refleja el equilibrio entre respuestas favorables y desfavorables, escaladas con respecto a un año base.

segments.src: ## Why Mood and Data Keep Pulling Apart
segments.tr: ## Why Mood and Data Keep Pulling Apart

segments.src: Economists have offered several explanations for the gap between sentiment and statistics.
segments.tr: Los economistas han ofrecido varias explicaciones para la brecha entre el sentimiento y las estadísticas.

segments.src: None of them is complete on its own, but together they paint a useful picture.
segments.tr: Ninguna de ellas es completa por sí sola, but juntas ofrecen un panorama útil.

segments.src: ### 1. Price levels matter more than inflation rates
segments.tr: ### 1. Price levels matter more than inflation rates

segments.src: Official statistics usually report the *rate* of inflation.
segments.tr: Las estadísticas oficiales suelen informar sobre la *tasa* de inflación.

segments.src: Households, however, experience the *level* of prices.
segments.tr: Los hogares, sin embargo, experimentan el *nivel* de precios.

segments.src: Even if inflation cools, groceries, rent, insurance, and utilities may still cost far more than they did a few years ago.
segments.tr: Even si la inflación se enfría, los comestibles, el alquiler, los seguros y los servicios públicos aún pueden costar mucho más que hace unos años.

segments.src: People tend to judge their well-being against what they remember paying, not against a rate of change.
segments.tr: Las personas tienden a juzgar su bienestar en comparación con lo que recuerdan haber pagado, no con una tasa de cambio.

segments.src: ### 2. Frequent purchases shape perception
segments.tr: ### 2. Frequent purchases shape perception

segments.src: Gasoline, food, and other everyday items are bought often and are highly visible.
segments.tr: La gasolina, los alimentos y otros artículos cotidianos se compran a menudo y son muy visibles.

segments.src: Big-ticket price moves in these categories can color a household's overall view of the economy more than a broad price index does.
segments.tr: Los movimientos de precios de gran envergadura en estas categorías pueden teñir la visión general de la economía que tiene un hogar más que un índice de precios amplio.

segments.src: ### 3. Borrowing costs bite
segments.tr: ### 3. Borrowing costs bite

segments.src: Higher interest rates affect mortgages, auto loans, and credit cards.
segments.tr: Los tipos de interés más altos afectan a las hipotecas, los préstamos para automóviles y las tarjetas de crédito.

segments.src: Someone who wants to buy a home or finance a car may feel squeezed even while the broader economy looks resilient.
segments.tr: Alguien que quiera comprar una casa o financiar un coche puede sentirse presionado incluso mientras la economía en general parece resiliente.

segments.src: That experience can weigh heavily on answers about "good times to buy."
segments.tr: Esa experiencia puede influir fuertemente en las respuestas sobre "buenos tiempos para comprar".

segments.src: ### 4. Uneven experiences hide behind averages
segments.tr: ### 4. Uneven experiences hide behind averages

segments.src: Aggregate data can look healthy while particular groups, such as renters, younger workers, or lower-income households, face a different reality.
segments.tr: Los datos agregados pueden parecer saludables mientras que grupos particulares, como los inquilinos, los trabajadores más jóvenes o los hogares de menores ingresos, se enfrentan a una realidad diferente.

segments.src: Sentiment surveys can pick up that unevenness in a way that headline employment or output figures do not.
segments.tr: Las encuestas de sentimiento pueden captar esa desigualdad de una manera que las cifras generales de empleo o producción no lo hacen.

segments.src: ### 5. Information and political filters
segments.tr: ### 5. Information and political filters

segments.src: Research has consistently shown that views about the economy can vary with political affiliation, media consumption, and recent news.
segments.tr: La investigación ha demostrado sistemáticamente que las opiniones sobre la economía pueden variar con la afiliación política, el consumo de medios y las noticias recientes.

segments.src: The same data can be read very differently depending on the lens.
segments.tr: Los mismos datos pueden leerse de manera muy diferente dependiendo de la lente.

segments.src: ## Why Expectations Matter for the Fed
segments.tr: ## Why Expectations Matter for the Fed

segments.src: The most closely watched part of the report for policymakers may not be the headline index at all.
segments.tr: La parte del informe que los responsables de la formulación de políticas siguen más de cerca puede no ser el índice principal en absoluto.

segments.src: It is the inflation expectations component.
segments.tr: Es el componente de las expectativas de inflación.

segments.src: Central banks generally believe that what people *expect* inflation to be can influence what inflation actually becomes.
segments.tr: Los bancos centrales creen generalmente que lo que la gente *espera* que sea la inflación puede influir en lo que la inflación realmente llega a ser.

segments.src: If households expect prices to rise faster, they may push for higher wages, accept price increases more readily, or move purchases forward.
segments.tr: Si los hogares esperan que los precios suban más rápido, pueden presionar para obtener salarios más altos, aceptar subidas de precios más fácilmente o adelantar sus compras.

segments.src: Businesses that expect rising costs may raise prices sooner.
segments.tr: Las empresas que esperan costos crecientes pueden subir los precios antes.

segments.src: Over time, these behaviors can make elevated inflation more persistent.
segments.tr: Con el tiempo, estos comportamientos pueden hacer que la inflación elevada sea más persistente.

segments.src: That is why a move in year-ahead expectations toward 4.6% draws attention.
segments.tr: Por eso llama la atención un movimiento en las expectativas a un año vista hacia el 4.6%.

segments.src: Several caveats apply:
segments.tr: Se aplican varias salvedades:

segments.src: - **Short-term expectations are noisy.** Year-ahead figures can swing with gasoline prices and news headlines, and they often overstate where inflation eventually settles.
segments.tr: - **Las expectativas a corto plazo son ruidosas.** Las cifras a un año vista pueden oscilar con los precios de la gasolina y los titulares de las noticias, y a menudo exageran dónde se estabiliza finalmente la inflación.

segments.src: - **Longer-term expectations matter more.** The Federal Reserve typically watches whether expectations five to ten years out remain "anchored" near its stated 2% goal. A rise there would be considered more concerning than a short-run jump.
segments.tr: - **Las expectativas a más largo plazo importan más.** La Reserva Federal suele vigilar si las expectativas a cinco o diez años se mantienen "ancladas" cerca de su objetivo declarado del 2%. Un aumento allí se consideraría más preocupante que un salto a corto plazo.

segments.src: - **Survey and market measures can disagree.** Policymakers compare household surveys with market-based indicators and other surveys of professional forecasters before drawing conclusions.
segments.tr: - **Las medidas de encuestas y mercado pueden disentir.** Los responsables políticos comparan las encuestas de hogares con indicadores basados en el mercado y otras encuestas de pronosticadores profesionales antes de sacar conclusiones.

segments.src: ## What to Watch Next
segments.tr: ## What to Watch Next

segments.src: A single monthly reading does not define a trend.
segments.tr: Una sola lectura mensual no define una tendencia.

segments.src: Readers who want to understand where sentiment may go from here could keep an eye on:
segments.tr: Los lectores que quieran entender hacia dónde puede ir el sentimiento a partir de ahora podrían vigilar:

segments.src: 1. **Gasoline and grocery prices**, which tend to feed quickly into household expectations.
segments.tr: 1. **Los precios de la gasolina y los comestibles**, que tienden a alimentar rápidamente las expectativas de los hogares.

segments.src: 2. **Labor market conditions**, since job security is a major driver of confidence.
segments.tr: 2. **Las condiciones del mercado laboral**, ya que la seguridad laboral es un motor principal de la confianza.

segments.src: 3. **Longer-run inflation expectations**, which are more important to monetary policy than the one-year figure.
segments.tr: 3. **Las expectativas de inflación a más largo plazo**, que son más importantes para la política monetaria que la cifra a un año.

segments.src: 4. **Other confidence gauges**, such as the Conference Board's index, which uses a different methodology and sometimes tells a different story.
segments.tr: 4. **Otros indicadores de confianza**, como el índice del Conference Board, que utiliza una metodología diferente y a veces cuenta una historia diferente.

segments.src: ## The Bottom Line
segments.tr: ## The Bottom Line

segments.src: A sentiment reading near 48 is a signal about how people feel, and feelings are part of the economy.
segments.tr: Una lectura del sentimiento cercana a 48 es una señal sobre cómo se siente la gente, y los sentimientos son parte de la economía.

segments.src: Households that feel pessimistic may spend more cautiously, and expectations that drift higher can complicate the job of those responsible for price stability.
segments.tr: Los hogares que se sienten pesimistas pueden gastar con más cautela, y las expectativas que se desplazan al alza pueden complicar el trabajo de los responsables de la estabilidad de precios.

segments.src: At the same time, sentiment is not a forecast, and it has often been a poor predictor of near-term spending.
segments.tr: Al mismo tiempo, el sentimiento no es un pronóstico, y a menudo ha sido un mal predictor del gasto a corto plazo.

segments.src: The gap between the mood and the data is not necessarily a contradiction.
segments.tr: La brecha entre el estado de ánimo y los datos no es necesariamente una contradicción.

segments.src: It is a reminder that an economy is both a set of statistics and a set of lived experiences, and that policymakers have to take both seriously.
segments.tr: Es un recordatorio de que una economía es tanto un conjunto de estadísticas como un conjunto de experiencias vividas, y que los responsables políticos tienen que tomarse ambas cosas en serio.

fr.title: Une lecture du sentiment à 48,1 : Pourquoi les Américains se sentent plus pessimistes que les données ne le suggèrent

segments.src: When the University of Michigan released its final consumer sentiment reading for September, the headline number landed near 48.
segments.tr: Lorsque l'Université du Michigan a publié son dernier indice de confiance des consommateurs pour septembre, le chiffre principal s'est établi près de 48.

segments.src: By historical standards, that is a very low reading, the kind of level more often associated with deep recessions or acute inflation shocks than with an economy that is still adding jobs and growing.
segments.tr: Selon les normes historiques, il s'agit d'un chiffre très bas, le genre de niveau plus souvent associé à de profondes récessions ou à des chocs inflationnistes aigus qu'à une économie qui continue de créer des emplois et de croître.

segments.src: The survey also showed year-ahead inflation expectations climbing toward 4.6%.
segments.tr: L'enquête a également montré que les anticipations d'inflation pour l'année à venir grimpaient vers 4,6 %.

segments.src: For many observers, the pairing raises an old question: why does the mood of American households so often diverge from the hard economic data?
segments.tr: Pour de nombreux observateurs, ce rapprochement soulève une vieille question : pourquoi l'humeur des ménages américains diverge-t-elle si souvent des données économiques concrètes ?

segments.src: And, just as importantly, why do central bankers pay such close attention to it?
segments.tr: Et, tout aussi important, pourquoi les banquiers centraux y prêtent-ils une attention si particulière ?

segments.src: ## What the Index Actually Measures
segments.tr: ## Ce que l'indice mesure réellement

segments.src: The University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers asks a representative sample of households about their personal finances, their view of business conditions, and their buying plans.
segments.tr: Les enquêtes auprès des consommateurs de l'Université du Michigan interrogent un échantillon représentatif de ménages sur leurs finances personnelles, leur vision des conditions commerciales et leurs projets d'achat.

segments.src: Respondents are also asked what they expect to happen to prices over the next year and over the next five to ten years.
segments.tr: On demande également aux répondants ce qu'ils prévoient concernant l'évolution des prix au cours de l'année prochaine et des cinq à dix prochaines années.

segments.src: Two points are worth keeping in mind:
segments.tr: Deux points méritent d'être gardés à l'esprit :

segments.src: - **It measures perception, not activity.** The index captures how people feel, not how much they are spending or earning.
segments.tr: - **Il mesure la perception, pas l'activité.** L'indice capture ce que les gens ressentent, et non le montant qu'ils dépensent ou gagnent.

segments.src: - **It is a diffusion-style index.** A reading near 48 does not mean "48% of people are unhappy." It reflects the balance of favorable and unfavorable answers, scaled against a baseline year.
segments.tr: - **Il s'agit d'un indice de type diffusion.** Une lecture proche de 48 ne signifie pas que "48 % des gens sont mécontents". Il reflète l'équilibre entre les réponses favorables et défavorables, mis à l'échelle par rapport à une année de référence.

segments.src: ## Why Mood and Data Keep Pulling Apart
segments.tr: ## Pourquoi l'humeur et les données continuent de diverger

segments.src: Economists have offered several explanations for the gap between sentiment and statistics.
segments.tr: Les économistes ont proposé plusieurs explications pour le fossé entre le sentiment et les statistiques.

segments.src: None of them is complete on its own, but together they paint a useful picture.
segments.tr: Aucune d'entre elles n'est complète en soi, mais ensemble, elles dressent un tableau utile.

segments.src: ### 1. Price levels matter more than inflation rates
segments.tr: ### 1. Les niveaux de prix comptent plus que les taux d'inflation

segments.src: Official statistics usually report the *rate* of inflation.
segments.tr: Les statistiques officielles rapportent généralement le *taux* d'inflation.

segments.src: Households, however, experience the *level* of prices.
segments.tr: Les ménages, cependant, font l'expérience du *niveau* des prix.

segments.src: Even if inflation cools, groceries, rent, insurance, and utilities may still cost far more than they did a few years ago.
segments.tr: Même si l'inflation ralentit, l'épicerie, le loyer, l'assurance et les services publics peuvent toujours coûter beaucoup plus cher qu'il y a quelques années.

segments.src: People tend to judge their well-being against what they remember paying, not against a rate of change.
segments.tr: Les gens ont tendance à juger leur bien-être par rapport à ce dont ils se souviennent avoir payé, et non par rapport à un taux de variation.

segments.src: ### 2. Frequent purchases shape perception
segments.tr: ### 2. Les achats fréquents façonnent la perception

segments.src: Gasoline, food, and other everyday items are bought often and are highly visible.
segments.tr: L'essence, la nourriture et d'autres articles du quotidien sont achetés souvent et sont très visibles.

segments.src: Big-ticket price moves in these categories can color a household's overall view of the economy more than a broad price index does.
segments.tr: Les mouvements de prix importants dans ces catégories peuvent colorer la vision globale de l'économie d'un ménage plus qu'un large indice des prix ne le fait.

segments.src: ### 3. Borrowing costs bite
segments.tr: ### 3. Les coûts d'emprunt pèsent lourd

segments.src: Higher interest rates affect mortgages, auto loans, and credit cards.
segments.tr: Des taux d'intérêt plus élevés affectent les prêts hypothécaires, les prêts automobiles et les cartes de crédit.

segments.src: Someone who wants to buy a home or finance a car may feel squeezed even while the broader economy looks resilient.
segments.tr: Quelqu'un qui souhaite acheter une maison ou financer une voiture peut se sentir étranglé même si l'économie dans son ensemble semble résiliente.

segments.src: That experience can weigh heavily on answers about "good times to buy."
segments.tr: Cette expérience peut peser lourdement sur les réponses concernant les "bons moments pour acheter".

segments.src: ### 4. Uneven experiences hide behind averages
segments.tr: ### 4. Les expériences inégales se cachent derrière les moyennes

segments.src: Aggregate data can look healthy while particular groups, such as renters, younger workers, or lower-income households, face a different reality.
segments.tr: Les données agrégées peuvent sembler saines alors que des groupes particuliers, tels que les locataires, les jeunes travailleurs ou les ménages à faible revenu, font face à une réalité différente.

segments.src: Sentiment surveys can pick up that unevenness in a way that headline employment or output figures do not.
segments.tr: Les enquêtes de sentiment peuvent capter cette inégalité d'une manière que les chiffres globaux de l'emploi ou de la production ne font pas.

segments.src: ### 5. Information and political filters
segments.tr: ### 5. Filtres d'information et politiques

segments.src: Research has consistently shown that views about the economy can vary with political affiliation, media consumption, and recent news.
segments.tr: La recherche a constamment montré que les points de vue sur l'économie peuvent varier en fonction de l'affiliation politique, de la consommation médiatique et des actualités récentes.

segments.src: The same data can be read very differently depending on the lens.
segments.tr: Les mêmes données peuvent être lues très différemment selon le prisme utilisé.

segments.src: ## Why Expectations Matter for the Fed
segments.tr: ## Pourquoi les anticipations comptent pour la Fed

segments.src: The most closely watched part of the report for policymakers may not be the headline index at all.
segments.tr: La partie du rapport la plus surveillée par les décideurs politiques n'est peut-être pas du tout l'indice principal.

segments.src: It is the inflation expectations component.
segments.tr: Il s'agit de la composante des anticipations d'inflation.

segments.src: Central banks generally believe that what people *expect* inflation to be can influence what inflation actually becomes.
segments.tr: Les banques centrales croient généralement que ce que les gens *prévoient* comme inflation peut influencer ce que l'inflation devient réellement.

segments.src: If households expect prices to rise faster, they may push for higher wages, accept price increases more readily, or move purchases forward.
segments.tr: Si les ménages s'attendent à ce que les prix augmentent plus rapidement, ils peuvent faire pression pour des salaires plus élevés, accepter plus facilement les augmentations de prix ou avancer leurs achats.

segments.src: Businesses that expect rising costs may raise prices sooner.
segments.tr: Les entreprises qui anticipent une hausse des coûts peuvent augmenter leurs prix plus tôt.

segments.src: Over time, these behaviors can make elevated inflation more persistent.
segments.tr: Au fil du temps, ces comportements peuvent rendre une inflation élevée plus persistante.

segments.src: That is why a move in year-ahead expectations toward 4.6% draws attention.
segments.tr: C'est pourquoi une évolution des anticipations à un an vers 4,6 % attire l'attention.

segments.src: Several caveats apply:
segments.tr: Plusieurs mises en garde s'appliquent :

segments.src: - **Short-term expectations are noisy.** Year-ahead figures can swing with gasoline prices and news headlines, and they often overstate where inflation eventually settles.
segments.tr: - **Les anticipations à court terme sont bruyantes.** Les chiffres à un an peuvent fluctuer avec les prix de l'essence et les gros titres de l'actualité, et ils surestiment souvent le niveau où l'inflation finit par se stabiliser.

segments.src: - **Longer-term expectations matter more.** The Federal Reserve typically watches whether expectations five to ten years out remain "anchored" near its stated 2% goal. A rise there would be considered more concerning than a short-run jump.
segments.tr: - **Les anticipations à plus long terme comptent davantage.** La Réserve fédérale surveille généralement si les anticipations à cinq ou dix ans restent "ancrées" près de son objectif déclaré de 2 %. Une hausse à ce niveau serait considérée comme plus préoccupante qu'un saut à court terme.

segments.src: - **Survey and market measures can disagree.** Policymakers compare household surveys with market-based indicators and other surveys of professional forecasters before drawing conclusions.
segments.tr: - **Les mesures d'enquête et de marché peuvent diverger.** Les décideurs politiques comparent les enquêtes auprès des ménages avec des indicateurs basés sur le marché et d'autres enquêtes auprès de prévisionnistes professionnels avant de tirer des conclusions.

segments.src: ## What to Watch Next
segments.tr: ## Que surveiller ensuite

segments.src: A single monthly reading does not define a trend.
segments.tr: Une seule lecture mensuelle ne définit pas une tendance.

segments.src: Readers who want to understand where sentiment may go from here could keep an eye on:
segments.tr: Les lecteurs qui veulent comprendre où le sentiment pourrait aller à partir d'ici pourraient garder un œil sur :

segments.src: 1. **Gasoline and grocery prices**, which tend to feed quickly into household expectations.
segments.tr: 1. **Les prix de l'essence et de l'épicerie**, qui ont tendance à alimenter rapidement les anticipations des ménages.

segments.src: 2. **Labor market conditions**, since job security is a major driver of confidence.
segments.tr: 2. **Les conditions du marché du travail**, car la sécurité de l'emploi est un moteur majeur de la confiance.

segments.src: 3. **Longer-run inflation expectations**, which are more important to monetary policy than the one-year figure.
segments.tr: 3. **Les anticipations d'inflation à plus long terme**, qui sont plus importantes pour la politique monétaire que le chiffre à un an.

segments.src: 4. **Other confidence gauges**, such as the Conference Board's index, which uses a different methodology and sometimes tells a different story.
segments.tr: 4. **D'autres jauges de confiance**, telles que l'indice du Conference Board, qui utilise une méthodologie différente et raconte parfois une histoire différente.

segments.src: ## The Bottom Line
segments.tr: ## L'essentiel

segments.src: A sentiment reading near 48 is a signal about how people feel, and feelings are part of the economy.
segments.tr: Une lecture du sentiment proche de 48 est un signal sur ce que les gens ressentent, et les sentiments font partie de l'économie.

segments.src: Households that feel pessimistic may spend more cautiously, and expectations that drift higher can complicate the job of those responsible for price stability.
segments.tr: Les ménages qui se sentent pessimistes peuvent dépenser plus prudemment, et les anticipations qui dérivent à la hausse peuvent compliquer le travail de ceux qui sont responsables de la stabilité des prix.

segments.src: At the same time, sentiment is not a forecast, and it has often been a poor predictor of near-term spending.
segments.tr: En même temps, le sentiment n'est pas une prévision, et il a souvent été un mauvais prédicteur des dépenses à court terme.

segments.src: The gap between the mood and the data is not necessarily a contradiction.
segments.tr: Le fossé entre l'humeur et les données n'est pas nécessairement une contradiction.

segments.src: It is a reminder that an economy is both a set of statistics and a set of lived experiences, and that policymakers have to take both seriously.
segments.tr: C'est un rappel qu'une économie est à la fois un ensemble de statistiques et un ensemble d'expériences vécues, et que les décideurs politiques doivent prendre les deux au sérieux.

segments.src: ## Why Mood and Data Keep Pulling Apart

segments.src: Economists have offered several explanations for the gap between sentiment and statistics.

segments.src: ### 1. Price levels matter more than inflation rates
segments.tr: ### 1. インフレ率よりも物価水準が重要である

segments.src: Official statistics usually report the *rate* of inflation.
segments.tr: 公式統計は通常、インフレの*率*を報告する。

segments.src: Households, however, experience the *level* of prices.
segments.tr: しかし、家計が経験するのは物価の*水準*である。

segments.src: Even if inflation cools, groceries, rent, insurance, and utilities may still cost far more than they did a few years ago.
segments.tr: たとえインフレが和らいだとしても、食料品、家賃、保険、光熱費は、数年前よりもはるかに高いままである可能性がある。

segments.src: People tend to judge their well-being against what they remember paying, not against a rate of change.
segments.tr: 人々は、変化率に対してではなく、過去に支払った記憶がある金額に対して自分たちの経済的幸福度を判断する傾向がある。

segments.src: ### 2. Frequent purchases shape perception
segments.tr: ### 2. 頻繁な買い物が認識を形作る

segments.src: Gasoline, food, and other everyday items are bought often and are highly visible.
segments.tr: ガソリン、食料品、その他の日常品は頻繁に購入され、非常に目につきやすい。

segments.src: Big-ticket price moves in these categories can color a household's overall view of the economy more than a broad price index does.
segments.tr: これらカテゴリにおける大きな価格変動は、広範な物価指数が示す以上に、経済に対する家計の全体的な見方を色濃く染めることがある。

segments.src: ### 3. Borrowing costs bite
segments.tr: ### 3. 借入コストの重み

segments.src: Higher interest rates affect mortgages, auto loans, and credit cards.
segments.tr: 金利上昇は住宅ローン、自動車ローン、クレジットカードに影響を与える。

segments.src: Someone who wants to buy a home or finance a car may feel squeezed even while the broader economy looks resilient.
segments.tr: 家を買いたい、あるいは車の融資を受けたいと考えている人は、より広い経済が強靭に見えるときであっても、圧迫感を感じるかもしれない。

segments.src: That experience can weigh heavily on answers about "good times to buy."
segments.tr: その経験は、「購入するのに良い時期」に関する回答に重くのしかかることがある。

segments.src: ### 4. Uneven experiences hide behind averages
segments.tr: ### 4. 平均値の裏に隠れた不均一な経験

segments.src: Aggregate data can look healthy while particular groups, such as renters, younger workers, or lower-income households, face a different reality.
segments.tr: 集計データは健全に見える一方で、賃貸生活者、若い労働者、低所得世帯といった特定のグループは異なる現実に直面している。

segments.src: ### 5. Information and political filters

segments.src: ## Why Expectations Matter for the Fed
segments.tr: ## FRBにとって期待が重要である理由

segments.src: The most closely watched part of the report for policymakers may not be the headline index at all.
segments.tr: 政策立案者にとってこの報告書で最も注目される部分は、見出しの指数そのものではないかもしれない。

segments.src: It is the inflation expectations component.
segments.tr: それはインフレ期待の構成要素である。

segments.src: Central banks generally believe that what people *expect* inflation to be can influence what inflation actually becomes.
segments.tr: 中央銀行は一般的に、人々がインフレについて*予想*することが、実際のインフレがどうなるかに影響を与えると信じている。

segments.src: If households expect prices to rise faster, they may push for higher wages, accept price increases more readily, or move purchases forward.
segments.tr: 家計が物価のより急速な上昇を予想する場合、より高い賃金を求めたり、値上げをより容易に受け入れたり、購入を前倒ししたりするかもしれない。

segments.src: Businesses that expect rising costs may raise prices sooner.
segments.tr: コスト上昇を予想する企業は、より早く値上げを行うかもしれない。

segments.src: Over time, these behaviors can make elevated inflation more persistent.
segments.tr: 時間が経つにつれて、これらの行動が高止まりしたインフレをより持続的なものにする可能性がある。

segments.src: That is why a move in year-ahead expectations toward 4.6% draws attention.
segments.tr: それが、1年先の期待が4.6%に向かう動きが注目を集める理由である。

segments.src: Several caveats apply:
segments.tr: いくつかの注意点が適用される：

segments.src: - **Short-term expectations are noisy.** Year-ahead figures can swing with gasoline prices and news headlines, and they often overstate where inflation eventually settles.
segments.tr: - **短期的な期待はノイズが多い。** 1年先の数値はガソリン価格やニュースの見出しによって変動し、インフレが最終的に落ち着く水準を過大評価することが多い。

segments.src: - **Longer-term expectations matter more.** The Federal Reserve typically watches whether expectations five to ten years out remain "anchored" near its stated 2% goal. A rise there would be considered more concerning than a short-run jump.
segments.tr: - **長期的な期待の方が重要である。** 連邦準備制度（FRB）は通常、5〜10年先の期待が目標とする2%近辺に「固定（アンコード）」されたままかどうかを注視している。そこの上昇は、短期的な急上昇よりも懸念されるものとみなされる。

segments.src: - **Survey and market measures can disagree.** Policymakers compare household surveys with market-based indicators and other surveys of professional forecasters before drawing conclusions.
segments.tr: - **調査と市場の尺度は意見が分かれることがある。** 政策立案者は、結論を下す前に、家計調査を市場ベースの指標や専門予測者の他の調査と比較する。

segments.tr: 48近辺のセンチメント・リーディングは、人々の気分についてのシグナルであり、気分は経済の一部である。

segments.src: Households that feel pessimistic may spend more cautiously, and expectations that drift higher can complicate the job of those responsible for price stability.
segments.tr: 悲観的に感じる家計はより慎重にお金を使う可能性があり、上向きに漂う期待は物価安定に責任を持つ人々の仕事を複雑にする可能性がある。

segments.src: At the same time, sentiment is not a forecast, and it has often been a poor predictor of near-term spending.
segments.tr: 同時に、センチメントは予測ではなく、短期的な支出の優れた予測因子ではないことが多い。

segments.src: The gap between the mood and the data is not necessarily a contradiction.
segments.tr: ムードとデータの間のギャップは、必ずしも矛盾ではない。

segments.src: It is a reminder that an economy is both a set of statistics and a set of lived experiences, and that policymakers have to take both seriously.
segments.tr: それは、経済が一連の統計であると同時に一連の実際の経験でもあること、そして政策立案者の双方がそれを真剣に受け止めなければならないことを思い出させるものである。

de.title: Eine Stimmungsmessung von 48.1: Warum sich Amerikaner düsterer fühlen, als die Daten vermuten lassen

segments.src: When the University of Michigan released its final consumer sentiment reading for September, the headline number landed near 48.
segments.tr: Als die University of Michigan ihren endgültigen Verbraucherstimmungsindex für September veröffentlichte, landete der Hauptwert bei fast 48.

segments.src: By historical standards, that is a very low reading, the kind of level more often associated with deep recessions or acute inflation shocks than with an economy that is still adding jobs and growing.
segments.tr: Nach historischen Maßstäben ist das ein sehr niedriger Wert, wie er sonst eher mit tiefen Rezessionen oder akuten Inflationsschocks assoziiert wird als mit einer Wirtschaft, die weiterhin Arbeitsplätze schafft und wächst.

segments.src: The survey also showed year-ahead inflation expectations climbing toward 4.6%.
segments.tr: Die Umfrage zeigte zudem, dass die Inflationserwartungen für das kommende Jahr auf 4.6% kletterten.

segments.src: For many observers, the pairing raises an old question: why does the mood of American households so often diverge from the hard economic data?
segments.tr: Für viele Beobachter wirft diese Kombination eine alte Frage auf: Warum weicht die Stimmung der amerikanischen Haushalte so oft von den harten Wirtschaftsdaten ab?

segments.src: And, just as importantly, why do central bankers pay such close attention to it?
segments.tr: Und, was ebenso wichtig ist, warum schenken Zentralbanker ihr so viel Aufmerksamkeit?

segments.src: ## What the Index Actually Measures
segments.tr: ## Was der Index tatsächlich misst

segments.src: The University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers asks a representative sample of households about their personal finances, their view of business conditions, and their buying plans.
segments.tr: Die University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers befragt eine repräsentative Stichprobe von Haushalten zu ihren persönlichen Finanzen, ihrer Sicht auf die geschäftlichen Bedingungen und ihren Kaufplänen.

segments.src: Respondents are also asked what they expect to happen to prices over the next year and over the next five to ten years.
segments.tr: Die Befragten werden außerdem gefragt, wie sich die Preise nach ihrer Einschätzung im nächsten Jahr sowie in den nächsten fünf bis zehn Jahren entwickeln werden.

segments.src: Two points are worth keeping in mind:
segments.tr: Zwei Punkte sollte man im Hinterkopf behalten:

segments.src: - **It measures perception, not activity.** The index captures how people feel, not how much they are spending or earning.
segments.tr: - **Er misst die Wahrnehmung, nicht die Aktivität.** Der Index erfasst, wie sich die Menschen fühlen, nicht, wie viel sie ausgeben oder verdienen.

segments.src: - **It is a diffusion-style index.** A reading near 48 does not mean "48% of people are unhappy." It reflects the balance of favorable and unfavorable answers, scaled against a baseline year.
segments.tr: - **Es handelt sich um einen Index im Diffusionsstil.** Ein Wert nahe 48 bedeutet nicht, dass "48% der Menschen unglücklich sind". Er spiegelt das Verhältnis von günstigen und ungünstigen Antworten wider, skaliert gegen ein Basisjahr.

segments.src: ## Why Mood and Data Keep Pulling Apart
segments.tr: ## Warum Stimmung und Daten weiter auseinanderdriften

segments.src: Economists have offered several explanations for the gap between sentiment and statistics.
segments.tr: Ökonomen haben verschiedene Erklärungen für die Kluft zwischen Stimmung und Statistik angeboten.

segments.src: None of them is complete on its own, but together they paint a useful picture.
segments.tr: Keine davon ist für sich genommen vollständig, aber zusammen ergeben sie ein nützliches Bild.

segments.src: ### 1. Price levels matter more than inflation rates
segments.tr: ### 1. Preisniveaus sind wichtiger als Inflationsraten

segments.src: Official statistics usually report the *rate* of inflation.
segments.tr: Offizielle Statistiken berichten gewöhnlich über die *Rate* der Inflation.

segments.src: Households, however, experience the *level* of prices.
segments.tr: Haushalte erleben jedoch das *Niveau* der Preise.

segments.src: Even if inflation cools, groceries, rent, insurance, and utilities may still cost far more than they did a few years ago.
segments.tr: Selbst wenn sich die Inflation abkühlt, kosten Lebensmittel, Miete, Versicherungen und Nebenkosten möglicherweise immer noch viel mehr als noch vor ein paar Jahren.

segments.src: People tend to judge their well-being against what they remember paying, not against a rate of change.
segments.tr: Die Menschen neigen dazu, ihr Wohlbefinden an dem zu messen, was sie ihrer Erinnerung nach bezahlt haben, und nicht an einer Veränderungsrate.

segments.src: ### 2. Frequent purchases shape perception
segments.tr: ### 2. Häufige Käufe prägen die Wahrnehmung

segments.src: Gasoline, food, and other everyday items are bought often and are highly visible.
segments.tr: Benzin, Lebensmittel und andere Artikel des täglichen Bedarfs werden oft gekauft und sind sehr sichtbar.

segments.src: Big-ticket price moves in these categories can color a household's overall view of the economy more than a broad price index does.
segments.tr: Preisschwankungen bei Anschaffungen mit hohem Wert in diesen Kategorien können die Gesamtsicht eines Haushalts auf die Wirtschaft stärker färben als ein breiter Preisindex.

segments.src: ### 3. Borrowing costs bite
segments.tr: ### 3. Kreditkosten schmerzen

segments.src: Higher interest rates affect mortgages, auto loans, and credit cards.
segments.tr: Höhere Zinssätze wirken sich auf Hypotheken, Autokredite und Kreditkarten aus.

segments.src: Someone who wants to buy a home or finance a car may feel squeezed even while the broader economy looks resilient.
segments.tr: Jemand, der ein Haus kaufen oder ein Auto finanzieren möchte, fühlt sich möglicherweise unter Druck, selbst wenn die Gesamtwirtschaft widerstandsfähig wirkt.

segments.src: That experience can weigh heavily on answers about "good times to buy."
segments.tr: Diese Erfahrung kann Antworten nach "guten Kaufzeitpunkten" stark belasten.

segments.src: ### 4. Uneven experiences hide behind averages
segments.tr: ### 4. Ungleiche Erfahrungen verbergen sich hinter Durchschnittswerten

segments.src: Aggregate data can look healthy while particular groups, such as renters, younger workers, or lower-income households, face a different reality.
segments.tr: Aggregierte Daten können gesund aussehen, während bestimmte Gruppen wie Mieter, jüngere Arbeitnehmer oder Haushalte mit niedrigerem Einkommen mit einer anderen Realität konfrontiert sind.

segments.src: Sentiment surveys can pick up that unevenness in a way that headline employment or output figures do not.
segments.tr: Stimmungsumfragen können diese Ungleichmäßigkeit auf eine Weise erfassen, wie es Beschäftigungs- oder Produktionszahlen nicht tun.

segments.src: ### 5. Information and political filters
segments.tr: ### 5. Informations- und politische Filter

segments.src: Research has consistently shown that views about the economy can vary with political affiliation, media consumption, and recent news.
segments.tr: Untersuchungen haben konsistent gezeigt, że Ansichten über die Wirtschaft mit der politischen Zugehörigkeit, dem Medienkonsum und den jüngsten Nachrichten variieren können.

segments.src: The same data can be read very differently depending on the lens.
segments.tr: Dieselbigen Daten können je nach Brille sehr unterschiedlich gelesen werden.

segments.src: ## Why Expectations Matter for the Fed
segments.tr: ## Warum Erwartungen für die Fed wichtig sind

segments.src: The most closely watched part of the report for policymakers may not be the headline index at all.
segments.tr: Der von politischen Entscheidungsträgern am genausten beobachtete Teil des Berichts ist vielleicht gar nicht der Hauptindex.

segments.src: It is the inflation expectations component.
segments.tr: Es ist die Komponente der Inflationserwartungen.

segments.src: Central banks generally believe that what people *expect* inflation to be can influence what inflation actually becomes.
segments.tr: Zentralbanken glauben im Allgemeinen, dass das, was die Menschen als Inflation *erwarten*, beeinflussen kann, was die Inflation tatsächlich wird.

segments.src: If households expect prices to rise faster, they may push for higher wages, accept price increases more readily, or move purchases forward.
segments.tr: Wenn Haushalte erwarten, dass die Preise schneller steigen, drängen sie möglicherweise auf höhere Löhne, akzeptieren Preiserhöhungen eher oder ziehen Käufe vor.

segments.src: Businesses that expect rising costs may raise prices sooner.
segments.tr: Unternehmen, die steigende Kosten erwarten, erhöhen möglicherweise früher die Preise.

segments.src: Over time, these behaviors can make elevated inflation more persistent.
segments.tr: Mit der Zeit können diese Verhaltensweisen eine erhöhte Inflation hartnäckiger machen.

segments.src: That is why a move in year-ahead expectations toward 4.6% draws attention.
segments.tr: Deshalb erregt eine Bewegung der Erwartungen für das kommende Jahr auf 4.6% Aufmerksamkeit.

segments.src: Several caveats apply:
segments.tr: Es gelten mehrere Einschränkungen:

segments.src: - **Short-term expectations are noisy.** Year-ahead figures can swing with gasoline prices and news headlines, and they often overstate where inflation eventually settles.
segments.tr: - **Kurzfristige Erwartungen sind rauschend.** Zahlen für das kommende Jahr können mit den Benzinpreisen und Schlagzeilen schwanken, und sie überschätzen oft, wo sich die Inflation schließlich einpendelt.

segments.src: - **Longer-term expectations matter more.** The Federal Reserve typically watches whether expectations five to ten years out remain "anchored" near its stated 2% goal. A rise there would be considered more concerning than a short-run jump.
segments.tr: - **Längerfristige Erwartungen sind wichtiger.** Die Federal Reserve beobachtet in der Regel, ob die Erwartungen auf Sicht von fünf bis zehn Jahren nahe ihrem erklärten Ziel von 2% "verankert" bleiben. Ein Anstieg dort würde als besorgniserregender angesehen werden als ein kurzfristiger Sprung.

segments.src: - **Survey and market measures can disagree.** Policymakers compare household surveys with market-based indicators and other surveys of professional forecasters before drawing conclusions.
segments.tr: - **Umfrage- und Marktwerte können voneinander abweichen.** Politische Entscheidungsträger vergleichen Haushaltsumfragen mit marktbasierten Indikatoren und anderen Umfragen unter professionellen Prognostizierenden, bevor sie Schlussfolgerungen ziehen.

segments.src: ## What to Watch Next
segments.tr: ## Was als Nächstes zu beobachten ist

segments.src: A single monthly reading does not define a trend.
segments.tr: Ein einzelner Monatsmesswert definiert keinen Trend.

segments.src: Readers who want to understand where sentiment may go from here could keep an eye on:
segments.tr: Leser, die verstehen möchten, wohin sich die Stimmung von hier aus entwickeln könnte, können Folgendes im Auge behalten:

segments.src: 1. **Gasoline and grocery prices**, which tend to feed quickly into household expectations.
segments.tr: 1. **Benzin- und Lebensmittelpreise**, die dazu neigen, schnell in die Erwartungen der Haushalte einzufließen.

segments.src: 2. **Labor market conditions**, since job security is a major driver of confidence.
segments.tr: 2. **Arbeitsmarktbedingungen**, da die Arbeitsplatzsicherheit ein Haupttreiber des Vertrauens ist.

segments.src: 3. **Longer-run inflation expectations**, which are more important to monetary policy than the one-year figure.
segments.tr: 3. **Längerfristige Inflationserwartungen**, die für die Geldpolitik wichtiger sind als die Einjahreszahl.

segments.src: 4. **Other confidence gauges**, such as the Conference Board's index, which uses a different methodology and sometimes tells a different story.
segments.tr: 4. **Andere Vertrauensindikatoren**, wie der Index des Conference Board, der eine andere Methodik verwendet und manchmal eine andere Geschichte erzählt.

segments.src: ## The Bottom Line
segments.tr: ## Das Fazit

segments.src: A sentiment reading near 48 is a signal about how people feel, and feelings are part of the economy.
segments.tr: Ein Stimmungswert nahe 48 ist ein Signal dafür, wie sich die Menschen fühlen, und Gefühle sind Teil der Wirtschaft.

segments.src: Households that feel pessimistic may spend more cautiously, and expectations that drift higher can complicate the job of those responsible for price stability.
segments.tr: Haushalte, die sich pessimistisch fühlen, geben möglicherweise vorsichtiger Geld aus, und Erwartungen, die nach oben driften, können die Arbeit derer erschweren, die für Preisstabilität verantwortlich sind.

segments.src: At the same time, sentiment is not a forecast, and it has often been a poor predictor of near-term spending.
segments.tr: Gleichzeitig ist die Stimmung keine Prognose und war oft ein schlechter Prädiktor für die kurzfristigen Ausgaben.

segments.src: The gap between the mood and the data is not necessarily a contradiction.
segments.tr: Die Kluft zwischen Stimmung und Daten ist nicht unbedingt ein Widerspruch.

segments.src: It is a reminder that an economy is both a set of statistics and a set of lived experiences, and that policymakers have to take both seriously.
segments.tr: Sie ist eine Erinnerung daran, dass eine Wirtschaft sowohl aus einer Reihe von Statistiken als auch aus gelebten Erfahrungen besteht und dass politische Entscheidungsträger beide ernst nehmen müssen.

segments.src: Two points are worth keeping in mind:
segments.tr: Có hai điểm đáng lưu ý:

segments.src: - **It measures perception, not activity.** The index captures how people feel, not how much they are spending or earning.
segments.tr: - **Nó đo lường nhận thức, không phải hoạt động.** Chỉ số này nắm bắt cảm nhận của mọi người, không phải số tiền họ đang chi tiêu hay kiếm được.

segments.src: ## Why Mood and Data Keep Pulling Apart
segments.tr: ## Tại sao tâm trạng và dữ liệu tiếp tục tách rời nhau

segments.src: Economists have offered several explanations for the gap between sentiment and statistics.
segments.tr: Các nhà kinh tế đã đưa ra một số lời giải thích cho khoảng cách giữa tâm lý và thống kê.

segments.src: None of them is complete on its own, but together they paint a useful picture.
segments.tr: Không có lời giải thích nào là hoàn chỉnh nếu đứng một mình, nhưng khi kết hợp lại, chúng tạo thành một bức tranh hữu ích.

segments.src: ### 1. Price levels matter more than inflation rates
segments.tr: ### 1. Mức giá quan trọng hơn tỷ lệ lạm phát

segments.src: Official statistics usually report the *rate* of inflation.
segments.tr: Số liệu thống kê chính thức thường báo cáo *tỷ lệ* lạm phát.

segments.src: Households, however, experience the *level* of prices.
segments.tr: Tuy nhiên, các hộ gia đình lại trải nghiệm *mức* giá.

segments.src: Even if inflation cools, groceries, rent, insurance, and utilities may still cost far more than they did a few years ago.
segments.tr: Ngay cả khi lạm phát hạ nhiệt, thực phẩm, tiền thuê nhà, bảo hiểm và các dịch vụ tiện ích vẫn có thể đắt hơn nhiều so với vài năm trước.

segments.src: People tend to judge their well-being against what they remember paying, not against a rate of change.
segments.tr: Mọi người có xu hướng đánh giá sự thịnh vượng của mình dựa trên những gì họ nhớ đã chi trả, chứ không phải dựa trên tỷ lệ thay đổi.

segments.src: ### 2. Frequent purchases shape perception
segments.tr: ### 2. Các giao dịch mua thường xuyên định hình nhận thức

segments.src: Gasoline, food, and other everyday items are bought often and are highly visible.
segments.tr: Xăng dầu, thực phẩm và các mặt hàng hàng ngày khác được mua thường xuyên và có tính hiển thị cao.

segments.src: Big-ticket price moves in these categories can color a household's overall view of the economy more than a broad price index does.
segments.tr: Biến động giá lớn trong các danh mục này có thể tô điểm cho quan điểm tổng thể của hộ gia đình về nền kinh tế nhiều hơn so với một chỉ số giá diện rộng.

segments.src: ### 3. Borrowing costs bite
segments.tr: ### 3. Chi phí vay đè nặng

segments.src: Higher interest rates affect mortgages, auto loans, and credit cards.
segments.tr: Lãi suất cao hơn ảnh hưởng đến các khoản thế chấp, cho vay ô tô và thẻ tín dụng.

segments.src: Someone who wants to buy a home or finance a car may feel squeezed even while the broader economy looks resilient.
segments.tr: Ai muốn mua nhà hoặc vay mua ô tô có thể cảm thấy bị chèn ép ngay cả khi nền kinh tế rộng lớn hơn có vẻ kiên cường.

segments.src: That experience can weigh heavily on answers about "good times to buy."
segments.tr: Trải nghiệm đó có thể đè nặng lên các câu trả lời về "thời điểm tốt để mua hàng."

segments.src: ### 4. Uneven experiences hide behind averages
segments.tr: ### 4. Trải nghiệm không đồng đều ẩn sau các mức trung bình

segments.src: Aggregate data can look healthy while particular groups, such as renters, younger workers, or lower-income households, face a different reality.
segments.tr: Dữ liệu tổng hợp có thể trông khỏe mạnh trong khi các nhóm cụ thể, chẳng hạn như người thuê nhà, người lao động trẻ hoặc các hộ gia đình thu nhập thấp, phải đối mặt với một thực tế khác.

segments.src: Sentiment surveys can pick up that unevenness in a way that headline employment or output figures do not.
segments.tr: Các khảo sát tâm lý có thể nắm bắt sự không đồng đều đó theo cách mà các số liệu việc làm hoặc sản lượng tiêu đề không làm được.

segments.src: ### 5. Information and political filters
segments.tr: ### 5. Bộ lọc thông tin và chính trị

segments.src: Research has consistently shown that views about the economy can vary with political affiliation, media consumption, and recent news.
segments.tr: Nghiên cứu đã liên tục chỉ ra rằng quan điểm về nền kinh tế có thể thay đổi theo liên kết chính trị, mức độ tiếp cận truyền thông và tin tức gần đây.

segments.src: The same data can be read very differently depending on the lens.
segments.tr: Cùng một dữ liệu có thể được đọc theo những cách rất khác nhau tùy thuộc vào lăng kính.

segments.src: ## Why Expectations Matter for the Fed
segments.tr: ## Tại sao kỳ vọng lại quan trọng đối với Fed

segments.src: The most closely watched part of the report for policymakers may not be the headline index at all.
segments.tr: Phần được theo dõi sát sao nhất của báo cáo đối với các nhà hoạch định chính sách có thể không phải là chỉ số tiêu đề chút nào.

segments.src: It is the inflation expectations component.
segments.tr: Đó là thành phần kỳ vọng lạm phát.

segments.src: Central banks generally believe that what people *expect* inflation to be can influence what inflation actually becomes.
segments.tr: Các ngân hàng trung ương thường tin rằng những gì mọi người *kỳ vọng* lạm phát sẽ xảy ra có thể ảnh hưởng đến lạm phát thực tế trở thành gì.

segments.src: If households expect prices to rise faster, they may push for higher wages, accept price increases more readily, or move purchases forward.
segments.tr: Nếu các hộ gia đình kỳ vọng giá cả tăng nhanh hơn, họ có thể đòi hỏi mức lương cao hơn, chấp nhận tăng giá dễ dàng hơn hoặc đẩy mạnh việc mua sắm lên trước.

segments.src: Businesses that expect rising costs may raise prices sooner.
segments.tr: Các doanh nghiệp kỳ vọng chi phí tăng có thể tăng giá sớm hơn.

segments.src: Over time, these behaviors can make elevated inflation more persistent.
segments.tr: Theo thời gian, những hành vi này có thể làm cho lạm phát cao trở nên dai dẳng hơn.

segments.src: That is why a move in year-ahead expectations toward 4.6% draws attention.
segments.tr: Đó là lý do tại sao sự dịch chuyển trong kỳ vọng năm tới hướng tới 4.6% lại thu hút sự chú ý.

segments.src: Several caveats apply:
segments.tr: Một số lưu ý được áp dụng:

segments.src: - **Short-term expectations are noisy.** Year-ahead figures can swing with gasoline prices and news headlines, and they often overstate where inflation eventually settles.
segments.tr: - **Kỳ vọng ngắn hạn rất nhiễu động.** Các số liệu trong năm tới có thể dao động theo giá xăng và tiêu đề tin tức, và chúng thường phóng đại mức độ mà lạm phát cuối cùng sẽ ổn định ở đó.

segments.src: - **Longer-term expectations matter more.** The Federal Reserve typically watches whether expectations five to ten years out remain "anchored" near its stated 2% goal. A rise there would be considered more concerning than a short-run jump.
segments.tr: - **Kỳ vọng dài hạn quan trọng hơn.** Cục Dự trữ Liên bang thường theo dõi xem liệu kỳ vọng từ 5 đến 10 năm tới có tiếp tục "neo đậu" gần mục tiêu 2% đã công bố của họ hay không. Sự gia tăng ở đó sẽ được coi là đáng lo ngại hơn một cú nhảy vọt trong ngắn hạn.

segments.src: - **Survey and market measures can disagree.** Policymakers compare household surveys with market-based indicators and other surveys of professional forecasters before drawing conclusions.
segments.tr: - **Các biện pháp khảo sát và thị trường có thể mâu thuẫn nhau.** Các nhà hoạch định chính sách so sánh các cuộc khảo sát hộ gia đình với các chỉ báo dựa trên thị trường và các cuộc khảo sát khác của các nhà dự báo chuyên nghiệp trước khi đưa ra kết luận.

segments.src: ## What to Watch Next
segments.tr: ## Những gì cần theo dõi tiếp theo

segments.src: A single monthly reading does not define a trend.
segments.tr: Một kết quả đọc hàng tháng đơn lẻ không xác định được một xu hướng.

segments.src: Readers who want to understand where sentiment may go from here could keep an eye on:
segments.tr: Độc giả muốn hiểu tâm lý có thể đi đến đâu từ đây có thể theo dõi:

segments.src: 1. **Gasoline and grocery prices**, which tend to feed quickly into household expectations.
segments.tr: 1. **Giá xăng và thực phẩm**, những thứ có xu hướng ngấm nhanh vào kỳ vọng của hộ gia đình.

segments.src: 2. **Labor market conditions**, since job security is a major driver of confidence.
segments.tr: 2. **Điều kiện thị trường lao động**, vì an ninh việc làm là động lực chính của niềm tin.

segments.src: 3. **Longer-run inflation expectations**, which are more important to monetary policy than the one-year figure.
segments.tr: 3. **Kỳ vọng lạm phát dài hạn hơn**, quan trọng hơn đối với chính sách tiền tệ so với con số một năm.

segments.src: 4. **Other confidence gauges**, such as the Conference Board's index, which uses a different methodology and sometimes tells a different story.
segments.tr: 4. **Các chỉ số niềm tin khác**, chẳng hạn như chỉ số của Conference Board, sử dụng phương pháp luận khác và đôi khi kể một câu chuyện khác.

segments.src: ## The Bottom Line
segments.tr: ## Điểm mấu chốt

segments.src: A sentiment reading near 48 is a signal about how people feel, and feelings are part of the economy.
segments.tr: Một chỉ số tâm lý gần 48 là một tín hiệu về cảm xúc của con người, và cảm xúc là một phần của nền kinh tế.

segments.src: Households that feel pessimistic may spend more cautiously, and expectations that drift higher can complicate the job of those responsible for price stability.
segments.tr: Các hộ gia đình cảm thấy bi quan có thể chi tiêu thận trọng hơn, và kỳ vọng trôi dạt cao hơn có thể làm phức tạp thêm công việc của những người chịu trách nhiệm về sự ổn định giá cả.

segments.src: At the same time, sentiment is not a forecast, and it has often been a poor predictor of near-term spending.
segments.tr: Đồng thời, tâm lý không phải là dự báo, và nó thường là một công cụ dự báo kém đối với chi tiêu trong ngắn hạn.

segments.src: The gap between the mood and the data is not necessarily a contradiction.
segments.tr: Khoảng cách giữa tâm trạng và dữ liệu không nhất thiết là một mâu thuẫn.

segments.src: It is a reminder that an economy is both a set of statistics and a set of lived experiences, and that policymakers have to take both seriously.
segments.tr: Đó là lời nhắc nhở rằng một nền kinh tế vừa là một tập hợp các số liệu thống kê vừa là một tập hợp các trải nghiệm thực tế, và các nhà hoạch định chính sách phải coi trọng cả hai.
